2: For the music director. Of David. A psalm. A song. God will arise; his enemies will be scattered, and those who hate him will flee from before him.
3: As smoke is driven off, you will drive them off. As wax melts before fire, the wicked will perish before God.
4: But the righteous will be glad; they will exalt before God, and will rejoice with joy.
5: Sing to God, sing praises to his name. Lift up a song to the rider on the clouds—his name is Yah— and rejoice before him.
6: A father to orphans and a judge for widows is God in his holy habitation.
7: God settles the lonely in a home; he brings prisoners out into prosperity. But the rebellious abide in a barren land.
8: O God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the desert, Selah
9: the earth shook; the heavens also dripped rain at the presence of God who was at Sinai, at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
10: You caused abundant rain to fall, O God. When your inheritance was weary you revived it.
11: Your community dwelled in it. You provided in your goodness for the poor, O God.
12: The Lord gives the word. Great is the company of women who announce:
13: “The kings of armies flee, they flee, and she who remains at home divides the spoil.
14: Though you men lie down between the sheepfolds, you will be like the wings of a dove covered in silver and its pinions in yellow gold.”
15: When Shaddai scattered kings on it, on Zalmon it snowed.
16: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.
17: Why do you look with hostility, O many-peaked mountains? This mountain God desires for his dwelling. Yes, Yahweh will abide in it forever.
18: The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, with thousands doubled. The Lord is among them at Sinai, distinctive in victory.
19: You have ascended on high; you have led away captives. You have received gifts from among humankind, and even from the rebellious, so that Yah God may dwell there.
20: Blessed be the Lord. Daily he loads us with benefits, the God of our salvation. Selah
21: Our God is a God of deliverances, and to the Yahweh the Lord belong escapes from death.
22: But God will shatter the head of his enemies, the hairy scalp of the one who ⌞continues on⌟ in his guilt.
23: The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
24: so that your foot may shatter them bloody for the tongues of your dogs to have their share from the enemies.”
25: They have seen your processions, O God, the processions of my God, my king, distinctive in victory.
26: Singers went up front, those playing stringed instruments last, between them young women playing tambourines.
27: Bless God in the assemblies, Yahweh from the fountain of Israel.
28: There is little Benjamin ruling them, with the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali.
29: Your God has commanded your strength. Show yourself strong, O God, by what you perform for us.
30: Because your temple is above Jerusalem, kings will bring tribute to you.
31: Rebuke the beasts in the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, trampling the pieces of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in battles.
32: Ambassadors will come from Egypt; Cush will quickly stretch out her hands to God.
33: O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praise to the Lord, Selah
34: to the one who rides in the highest heavens of old. See, he gives forth his voice, a mighty voice.
35: Ascribe strength to God. His majesty is over Israel, and his strength is in the clouds.
36: Awesome are you, O God, from your sanctuary. The God of Israel, it is he who gives strength and might to the people. Blessed be God.
